jobAccepted202Response.description: Accepted. A JSON object containing job resource details of the accepted operation to obtain status and output of the progress.

okSingleJobResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing a job resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link.

okSingleJobOutputResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing a job output resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link.

errorResponse.description: Unexpected error. A JSON object containing error details of the issue while executing the operation.

badRequestResponse.description: Bad Request. A JSON object containing error details of the issue found while parsing a parameter value or name.

okArrayOfItemsResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing an "items" property populated with 0 or more elements with at least an Id property and the links array with at least the "self" link.

okSingleImageResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing an image resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link.

okDeleteImageResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing an image resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link. Only if it was successfully deleted.

okSingleSeriesResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing a series resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link.

okDeleteSeriesResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing a series resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link. Only if it was successfully deleted.

okSingleWorkingcopyResponse.description: OK. A JSON object containing a working copy resource representation with multiple properties and the links array with at least the "self" link.

In an Oracle RAC environment, this only applies if the blocker is on the same instance. A client requires SQL Administrator role to invoke this service.

parameters.name: q

Filtering enables efficient traversal of large collections.

200.description: All locks that are blocking other sessions.

post.summary: Create a PDB from PDB$SEED or XML
post.description: Create a pluggable database from PDB$SEED or from an XML metadata file accessible to the database instance. This service requires db.cdb.adminUser credentials to be set in the pool configuration. A client requires SQL Administrator role to invoke this service.

method.description: This property defines the type of operation. Depending on the method specified, other properties will be required in the payload.

adminName.description: The administrator username for the new PDB. This property is required when the method property is CREATE.

adminPwd.description: The administrator password for the new PDB. This property is required when the method property is CREATE.

pdb_name.description: The name of the new PDB. Relevant to both CREATE and PLUG method.

asClone.description: Indicate if 'AS CLONE' option should be used in the command to plug in a PDB. This property is applicable when the method property is PLUG but not required.

xmlFileName.description: The path of the XML metadata file to use when plugging-in a PDB.

copyAction.description: Indicate which copy option should be used in the command to plug in a PDB. This property is required when the method property is PLUG.

sourceFileNameConversions.description: This property is required when the method property is PLUG. As defined in the Oracle Multitenant Database documentation. Values can be a source filename convert pattern or NONE.

fileNameConversions.description: Relevant for create and plug operations. As defined in the  Oracle Multitenant Database documentation. Values can be a filename convert pattern or NONE.

unlimitedStorage.description: Relevant for create and plug operations. True for unlimited storage. Even when set to true, totalSize and tempSize MUST be specified in the request if method is CREATE.

reuseTempFile.description: Relevant for create and plug operations. True for temporary file reusage.

totalSize.description: Relevant for create and plug operations. Total size as defined in the Oracle Multitenant Database documentation. See size_clause description in Database SQL Language Reference documentation.

tempSize.description: Relevant for create and clone operations. Total size for temporary tablespace as defined in the Oracle Multitenant Database documentation. See size_clause description in Database SQL Language Reference documentation.

tdePassword.description: TDE password when applicable (optional). Can be used in create and plug operations.

tdeKeystorePath.description: TDE keystore path is required if the tdeImport flag is set to true. Can be used in  plug operations.

tdeSecret.description: TDE secret is required if the tdeImport flag is set to true. Can be used in plug operations.

The use of of Oracle Transparent Data Encryption is only supported in topologies where the database and Oracle REST Data Services are on the same host. reuseTempFile.description: Relevant for clone operations. True for temporary file reusage.

totalSize.description: Relevant for clone operations. Size of the tablespace. See size_clause description in Database SQL Language Reference documentation.

tempSize.description: Relevant for clone operations. Size of the temporary tablespace. See size_clause description in Database SQL Language Reference documentation.

DatabaseComponents.description: DBA_REGISTRY displays information about all components in the database that are loaded into the component registry. The component registry tracks components that can be separately loaded into the Oracle Database. When a SQL script loads the PL/SQL packages and other database objects for a component into the database, the script records the component name, status, and version. If scripts are used to upgrade/downgrade the dictionary elements for the component, then those scripts also record status and version information.

adr_home.description: Directory location of the Automatic Diagnostic Repository (ADR).

originating_timestamp.description: Date and time when the message was generated.

normalized_timestamp.description: Date and time when the message originated, normalized for clock drift to the Oracle Enterprise Manager repository time.

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that wrote the originating component, usually the domain of the organization.

component_id.description: ID of the product or component that originated the message.

host_address.description: IP of other network address of the originating host for the message.

message_type.description: Type of the message, indicating that a different type of response is required.

message_type_name.description: A text description of the corresponding message type value.

message_level.description: Level the message belongs to. Lower level values imply higher severity for errors.

message_level_name.description: A text description of the corresponding message level value.

message_group.description: Name of the group to which the message belongs.

client_id.description: ID of the client or security group that the message relates to.

process_id.description: ID of the process that originated the message.

thread_id.description: ID of the thread of the process that originated the message.

downstream_comp_id.description: ID of a component that the originating component is working with on the downstream (server) side.

execution_context_id.description: Identifies the thread of execution that the originating component participates in.

error_instance_id.description: ID of the instance where error occurred.

message_text.description: Fully formed and localized text of the message.

message_arguments.description: Arguments to be bound with the generic text of the message.

supplemental_attributes.description: Supplemental attributes that are specific to a message. This field contains the impacts for an incident type error message.

supplemental_details.description: Supplemental data that is specific to a particular program and error message required to complete the diagnosis.

record_id.description: Record number for the message (this value is same as the row number).

problem_key.description: Describes the key for the current problem that the message is associated with.

version.description: Oracle ARB logging standard version number for the message.

MonitoringSessionWaitsItem.description: This object represents a record from GV$SESSION_WAIT view. GV$SESSION_WAIT displays the current or last wait for each session. The list of attributes may vary depending on database version.

inst_id.description: Oracle Real Application Clusters instance number for which this data relates to. In a non-RAC database this number will be 1.

seq#.description: A number that uniquely identifies the current or last wait (incremented for each wait).

event.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the resource or event for which the session is waiting. If the session is not in a wait, then the resource or event for which the session most recently waited.

p1text.description: Description of the first wait event parameter.

p2text.description: Description of the second wait event parameter.

p3text.description: Description of the third wait event parameter.

wait_class_id.description: Identifier of the class of the wait event.

wait_class#.description: Number of the class of the wait event.

wait_class.description: Name of the class of the wait event.

wait_time.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the value is 0. If the session is not in a wait, then the value indicates the duration of the last wait.

seconds_in_wait.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the value is the amount of time waited for the current wait. If the session is not in a wait, then the value is the amount of time since the start of the last wait.

wait_time_micro.description: Amount of time waited (in microseconds). If the session is currently waiting, then the value is the time spent in the current wait. If the session is currently not in a wait, then the value is the amount of time waited in the last wait.

time_remaining_micro.description: Amount of time remaining remaining before a timeout. This field may indicate that a timeout has occurred, or that no timeout will occur.

time_since_last_wait_micro.description: Time elapsed since the end of the last wait (in microseconds). If the session is currently in a wait, then the value is 0.

MonitoringSessionsItem.description: This object represents a record from GV$SESSION view. GV$SESSION displays session information for each current session. The list of attributes may vary depending on database version.

inst_id.description: Oracle Real Application Clusters instance number for which this data relates to. In a non-RAC database this number will be 1.

serial#.description: Session serial number. Used to uniquely identify a session's objects. Guarantees that session-level commands are applied to the correct session objects if the session ends and another session begins with the same session ID.

paddr.description: Address of the process that owns the session.

ownerid.description: Identifier of the user who owns the migratable session.

taddr.description: Address of the transaction state object.

lockwait.description: Address of the lock the session is waiting for; NULL if none.

sql_address.description: Used with sql_hash_value to identify the SQL statement that is currently being executed.

sql_hash_value.description: Used with SQL_ADDRESS to identify the SQL statement that is currently being executed.

sql_id.description: SQL identifier of the SQL statement that is currently being executed.

sql_child_number.description: Child number of the SQL statement that is currently being executed.

sql_exec_start.description: Time when the execution of the SQL currently executed by this session started; NULL if SQL_ID is NULL.

sql_exec_id.description: SQL execution identifier; NULL if SQL_ID is NULL or if the execution of that SQL has not yet started.

prev_sql_addr.description: Used with PREV_HASH_VALUE to identify the last SQL statement executed.

prev_hash_value.description: Used with SQL_HASH_VALUE to identify the last SQL statement executed.

prev_sql_id.description: SQL identifier of the last SQL statement executed.

prev_child_number.description: Child number of the last SQL statement executed.

prev_exec_start.description: SQL execution start of the last executed SQL statement.

prev_exec_id.description: SQL execution identifier of the last executed SQL statement.

plsql_entry_object_id.description: Object ID of the top-most PL/SQL subprogram on the stack; NULL if there is no PL/SQL subprogram on the stack.

plsql_entry_subprogram_id.description: Subprogram ID of the top-most PL/SQL subprogram on the stack; NULL if there is no PL/SQL subprogram on the stack.

plsql_object_id.description: Object ID of the currently executing PL/SQL subprogram; NULL if executing SQL.

plsql_subprogram_id.description: Subprogram ID of the currently executing PL/SQL object; NULL if executing SQL.

module.description: Name of the currently executing module as set by calling the DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO.SET_MODULE procedure.

module_hash.description: Hash value of the MODULE column.

action.description: Name of the currently executing action as set by calling the DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO.SET_ACTION procedure.

action_hash.description: Hash value of the ACTION column.

client_info.description: Information set by the DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO.SET_CLIENT_INFO procedure.

fixed_table_sequence.description: This contains a number that increases every time the session completes a call to the database and there has been an intervening select from a dynamic performance table. This column can be used by performance monitors to monitor statistics in the database.

row_wait_obj#.description: Object ID for the table containing the row specified in row_wait_row#.

row_wait_file#.description: Identifier for the data file containing the row specified in row_wait_row#. This property is valid only if the session is currently waiting for another transaction to commit and the value of row_wait_obj# is not -1.

row_wait_block#.description: Identifier for the block containing the row specified in row_wait_row#. This property is valid only if the session is currently waiting for another transaction to commit and the value of row_wait_obj# is not -1.

row_wait_row#.description: Current row being locked. This property is valid only if the session is currently waiting for another transaction to commit and the value of row_wait_obj# is not -1.

last_call_et.description: If the session STATUS is currently ACTIVE, then the value represents the elapsed time (in seconds) since the session has become active. If the session STATUS is currently INACTIVE, then the value represents the elapsed time (in seconds) since the session has become inactive.

pdml_enabled.description: This column has been replaced by the PDML_STATUS column.

failover_type.description: Indicates whether and to what extent transparent application failover (TAF) is enabled for the session.

failover_method.description: Indicates the transparent application failover method for the session.

failed_over.description: Indicates whether the session is running in failover mode and failover has occurred (YES) or not (NO).

resource_consumer_group.description: Name of the session's current resource consumer group.

pdml_status.description: If ENABLED, the session is in a PARALLEL DML enabled mode. If DISABLED, PARALLEL DML enabled mode is not supported for the session. If FORCED, the session has been altered to force PARALLEL DML.

pddl_status.description: If ENABLED, the session is in a PARALLEL DDL enabled mode. If DISABLED, PARALLEL DDL enabled mode is not supported for the session. If FORCED, the session has been altered to force PARALLEL DDL.

pq_status.description: If ENABLED, the session is in a PARALLEL QUERY enabled mode. If DISABLED, PARALLEL QUERY enabled mode is not supported for the session. If FORCED, the session has been altered to force PARALLEL QUERY.

current_queue_duration.description: If queued (1), the current amount of time the session has been queued. If not currently queued, the value is 0.

blocking_session_status.description: This column provides details on whether there is a blocking session.

blocking_instance.description: Instance identifier of the blocking session. This column is valid only if BLOCKING_SESSION_STATUS has the value VALID.

blocking_session.description: Session identifier of the blocking session. This column is valid only if BLOCKING_SESSION_STATUS has the value VALID.

final_blocking_session_status.description: The final blocking session is the final element in the wait chain constructed by following the sessions that are blocked by one another starting with this session. In the case of a cyclical wait chain, one of the sessions in the wait chain will be chosen as the final blocker.

final_blocking_instance.description: Instance identifier of the final blocking session. This column is valid only if FINAL_BLOCKING_SESSION_STATUS has the value VALID.

final_blocking_session.description: Session identifier of the blocking session. This column is valid only if FINAL_BLOCKING_SESSION_STATUS has the value VALID.

event#.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the number of the resource or event for which the session is waiting. If the session is not in a wait, then the number of the resource or event for which the session most recently waited.

event.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the resource or event for which the session is waiting. If the session is not in a wait, then the resource or event for which the session most recently waited.

p1text.description: Description of the first wait event parameter.

wait_class#.description: Number of the class of the wait event.

wait_class.description: Name of the class of the wait event.

wait_time.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the value is 0. If the session is not in a wait, then the value indicates the duration of the last wait.

seconds_in_wait.description: If the session is currently waiting, then the value is the amount of time waited for the current wait. If the session is not in a wait, then the value is the amount of time since the start of the last wait.

wait_time_micro.description: Amount of time waited (in microseconds). If the session is currently waiting, then the value is the time spent in the current wait. If the session is currently not in a wait, then the value is the amount of time waited in the last wait.

time_remaining_micro.description: Amount of time remaining remaining before a timeout. This field may indicate that a timeout has occurred, or that no timeout will occur.

time_since_last_wait_micro.description: Time elapsed since the end of the last wait (in microseconds). If the session is currently in a wait, then the value is 0.

sql_trace.description: Indicates whether SQL tracing is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED).

sql_trace_waits.description: Indicates whether wait tracing is enabled (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

sql_trace_binds.description: Indicates whether bind tracing is enabled (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

sql_trace_plan_stats.description: Frequency at which row source statistics are dumped in the trace files for each cursor.

session_edition_id.description: Shows the value that, in the session, would be reported by sys_context('USERENV', 'SESSION_EDITION_ID').

creator_addr.description: Address of the creating process or circuit.

creator_serial#.description: Serial number of the creating process or circuit.

ecid.description: Execution context identifier (sent by Application Server).

sql_translation_profile_id.description: Object number of the SQL translation profile.

pga_tunable_mem.description: The amount of tunable PGA memory (in bytes).

shard_ddl_status.description: Indicates whether shard DDL is enabled in the current session (ENABLED) or not (DISABLED). This value is only relevant for the shard catalog database.

con_id.description: The ID of the container to which the data pertains.

external_name.description: External name of the database user. For enterprise users, returns the Oracle Internet Directory DN.

plsql_debugger_connected.description: Indicates whether the session is connected to a PL/SQL debugger.

inst_id.description: Oracle Real Application Clusters instance number for which this data relates to. In a non-RAC database this number will be 1.

sid.description: Identifier of the session processing the long-running operation. If multiple sessions are cooperating in the long-running operation, then SID corresponds to the main or master session.

target.description: Object on which the operation is carried out.

sofar.description: Units of work done so far for the operation specified in the OPNAME column.

totalwork.description: Total units of work for the operation specified in the OPNAME column.

last_update_time.description: Time when statistics were last updated for the operation.

time_remaining.description: Estimate (in seconds) of time remaining for the operation to complete.

elapsed_seconds.description: Number of elapsed seconds from the start of the operations.

username.description: User ID of the user performing the operation.

sql_hash_value.description: Used with SQL_ADDRESS to identify the SQL statement that is currently being executed.

sql_id.description: SQL identifier of the SQL statement that is currently being executed.

sql_plan_hash_value.description: Used with the value of the SQL_ADDRESS column to identify the SQL statement associated with the operation.

sql_exec_id.description: SQL execution identifier; NULL if SQL_ID is NULL or if the execution of that SQL has not yet started.

sql_plan_line_id.description: SQL plan line ID corresponding to the long operation; NULL if the long operation is not associated with a line of the execution plan.

sql_plan_operation.description: Plan operation name; NULL if SQL_PLAN_LINE_ID is NULL.

sql_plan_options.description: Plan operation options; NULL if SQL_PLAN_LINE_ID is NULL.

qcsid.description: Session identifier of the parallel coordinator.

object_name.description: Name of the procedure or function.

object_id.description: Dictionary object number of the object.

overload.description: Indicates the nth overloading ordered by its appearance in the source; otherwise, it is NULL.

argument_name.description: If the argument is a scalar type, then the argument name is the name of the argument. A null argument name is used to denote a function return. If the function return or argument is a composite type, this view will have one row for each attribute of the composite type. Attributes are recursively expanded if they are composite.

position.description: If DATA_LEVEL is zero, then this column holds the position of this item in the argument list, or zero for a function return value.If DATA_LEVEL is greater than zero, then this column holds the position of this item with respect to its siblings at the same DATA_LEVEL. So, for a referenced record field, this is the index of the field within the record. For a referenced collection element, this is 1 (because collection elements do not have siblings.)

sequence.description: Defines the sequential order of the argument and its attributes. Argument sequence starts from 1. Return type and its recursively expanded (preorder tree walk) attributes will come first, and each argument with its recursively expanded (preorder tree walk) attributes will follow.

data_level.description: Nesting depth of the argument for composite types.

defaulted.description: Specifies whether or not the argument is defaulted.

in_out.description: Direction of the argument: IN, OUT, IN/OUT.

data_precision.description: Length in decimal digits (NUMBER) or binary digits (FLOAT).

data_scale.description: Digits to the right of the decimal point in a number.

character_set_name.description: Character set name for the argument.

type_owner.description: Owner of the type of the argument.

type_name.description: Name of the type of the argument. If the type is a package local type (that is, it is declared in a package specification), then this column displays the name of the package.

type_subname.description: Relevant only for package local types. Displays the name of the type declared in the package identified in the TYPE_NAME column.

type_link.description: Relevant only for package local types when the package identified in the TYPE_NAME column is a remote package. This column displays the database link used to refer to the remote package.

type_object_type.description: Displays the type of the type described by the TYPE_OWNER, TYPE_NAME, and TYPE_SUBNAME columns.

pls_type.description: For numeric arguments, the name of the PL/SQL type of the argument. Null otherwise.

char_used.description: Indicates whether the byte limit (B) or char limit (C) is official for the string.

owner.description: Owner of the table, view, or cluster.

table_name.description: Name of the table, view, or cluster.

data_type_mod.description: Data type modifier of the column.

data_type_owner.description: Owner of the data type of the column.

data_precision.description: Decimal precision for NUMBER data type; binary precision for FLOAT data type; NULL for all other data types.

data_scale.description: Digits to the right of the decimal point in a number.

nullable.description: Indicates whether a column allows NULLs. The value is N if there is a NOT NULL constraint on the column or if the column is part of a PRIMARY KEY. The constraint should be in an ENABLE VALIDATE state.

column_id.description: Sequence number of the column as created.

default_length.description: Length of the default value for the column.

num_distinct.description: Number of distinct values in the column.

density.description: If a histogram is available on COLUMN_NAME, then this column displays the selectivity of a value that spans fewer than 2 endpoints in the histogram. It does not represent the selectivity of values that span 2 or more endpoints. If a histogram is not available on COLUMN_NAME, then the value of this column is 1/NUM_DISTINCT.

num_nulls.description: Number of NULLs in the column.

num_buckets.description: Number of buckets in the histogram for the column.

last_analyzed.description: Date on which this column was most recently analyzed.

sample_size.description: Sample size used in analyzing this column.

char_col_decl_length.description: Declaration length of the character type column.

global_stats.description: GLOBAL_STATS will be YES if statistics are gathered or incrementally maintained, otherwise it will be NO.

user_stats.description: Indicates whether statistics were entered directly by the user (YES) or not (NO).

avg_col_len.description: Average length of the column (in bytes).

char_length.description: Displays the length of the column in characters.

char_used.description: Indicates that the column uses BYTE length semantics (B) or CHAR length semantics (C), or whether the data type is not any of the following (NULL): CHAR, VARCHAR2, NCHAR, NVARCHAR2.

v80_fmt_image.description: Indicates whether the column data is in release 8.0 image format (YES) or not (NO).

data_upgraded.description: Indicates whether the column data has been upgraded to the latest type version format (YES) or not (NO).

default_on_null.description: Indicates whether the column has DEFAULT ON NULL semantics (YES) or not (NO).

identity_column.description: Indicates whether this is an identity column (YES) or not (NO).

sensitive_column.description: Indicates whether this is a sensitive column (YES) or not (NO).

evaluation_edition.description: Name of the edition in which editioned objects referenced in an expression column are resolved.

unusable_before.description: Name of the oldest edition in which the index may be used as part of a query plan.

unusable_beginning.description: Name of the edition for which the index may not be used as part of a query plan in this edition or any of its descendants.

collation.description: Collation for the column. Only applies to columns with character data types.

DatabaseObjectsIndexesItem.description: Describes an index in the database.

uniqueness.description: Indicates whether the index is unique (UNIQUE) or nonunique (NONUNIQUE).

compression.description: The type of compression being used for the index.

prefix_length.description: Number of columns in the prefix of the compression key.

tablespace_name.description: Name of the tablespace containing the index.

min_extents.description: Minimum number of extents allowed in the segment.

max_extents.description: Maximum number of extents allowed in the segment.

pct_threshold.description: Threshold percentage of block space allowed per index entry.

include_column.description: Column ID of the last column to be included in index-organized table primary key (non-overflow) index.

freelist_groups.description: Number of freelist groups allocated to this segment.

pct_free.description: Minimum percentage of free space in a block.

avg_data_blocks_per_key.description: Average number of data blocks in the table that are pointed to by a distinct value in the index rounded to the nearest integer.

ityp_owner.description: For a domain index, the owner of the indextype.

join_index.description: Indicates whether the index is a join index (YES) or not (NO).

dropped.description: Indicates whether redundant primary key columns are eliminated from secondary indexes on index-organized tables (YES) or not (NO).

visibility.description: Indicates whether the index is VISIBLE or INVISIBLE to the optimizer.

domidx_management.description: If this is a domain index, indicates whether the domain index is system-managed (SYSTEM_MANAGED) or user-managed (USER_MANAGED).

segment_created.description: Indicates whether the index segment has been created (YES) or not (NO).

DatabaseObjectsPartitionsItem.description: This object represents partition-level partitioning information, partition storage parameters, and partition statistics generated by the DBMS_STATS package for a partition in the database. The list of attributes may vary depending on database version.

composite.description: Indicates whether the table is composite-partitioned (YES) or not (NO).

subpartition_count.description: If this is a composite partitioned table, the number of subpartitions in the partition.

high_value_length.description: Length of the partition bound value expression.

partition_position.description: Position of the partition within the table.

tablespace_name.description: Name of the tablespace containing the partition.

pct_free.description: Minimum percentage of free space in a block.

pct_used.description: Minimum percentage of used space in a block.

initial_extent.description: Size of the initial extent in bytes (for a range partition); size of the initial extent in blocks (for a composite partition).

next_extent.description: Size of secondary extents in bytes (for a range partition); size of secondary extents in blocks (for a composite partition).

min_extent.description: Minimum number of extents allowed in the segment.

max_extent.description: Maximum number of extents allowed in the segment.

max_size.description: Maximum number of blocks allowed in the segment.

freelists.description: Number of process freelists allocated in this segment.

freelist_groups.description: Number of freelist groups allocated in this segment.

logging.description: Indicates whether or not changes to the table are logged.

compression.description: Indicates the actual compression property for a partition of a simple partitioned table, or the default (if specified) for subpartitions for composite partitioned tables, otherwise NONE.

compress_for.description: Default compression for what kind of operations.

num_rows.description: Number of rows in the partition.

blocks.description: Number of used data blocks in the partition.

empty_blocks.description: Number of empty (never used) data blocks in the partition. This column is populated only if you collect statistics on the table using the DBMS_STATS package.

avg_space.description: Average amount of free space, in bytes, in a data block allocated to the partition.

chain_cnt.description: Number of rows in the partition that are chained from one data block to another, or which have migrated to a new block, requiring a link to preserve the old ROWID.

avg_row_len.description: Average length of a row in the partition (in bytes).

sample_size.description: Sample size used in analyzing this partition.

last_analyzed.description: Date on which this partition was most recently analyzed.

buffer_pool.description: Buffer pool to be used for the partition blocks.

flash_cache.description: Buffer pool to be used for the partition blocks.

cell_flash_cache.description: Cell flash cache hint to be used for partition blocks.

global_stats.description: GLOBAL_STATS will be YES if statistics are gathered or incrementally maintained, otherwise it will be NO.

user_stats.description: Indicates whether statistics were entered directly by the user (YES) or not (NO).

is_nested.description: Indicates whether this is a nested table partition (YES) or not (NO).

interval.description: Indicates whether the partition is in the interval section of an interval partitioned table (YES) or whether the partition is in the range section (NO).

segment_created.description: Indicates the actual segment creation property for a partition of a simple partitioned table, or the default (if specified) for subpartitions for composite partitioned tables, otherwise NONE.

indexing.description: Indicates the actual indexing property for a partition of a simple partitioned table, or the default (if specified) for subpartitions for composite partitioned tables, otherwise NONE.

read_only.description: Indicates the default setting for the partition.

inmemory.description: Indicates whether the In-Memory Column Store (IM column store) is enabled (ENABLED) or disabled (DISABLED) for this partition.

inmemory_priority.description: Indicates the priority for In-Memory Column Store (IM column store) population.

inmemory_distribute.description: Indicates how the IM column store is distributed in an Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) environment.

inmemory_compression.description: Indicates the compression level for the IM column store.

inmemory_duplicate.description: Indicates the duplicate setting for the IM column store in an Oracle RAC environment.

cellmemory.description: The value for columnar compression in the storage cell flash cache.

inmemory_service.description: Indicates how the IM column store is populated on various instances.

inmemory_service_name.description: Indicates the service name for the service on which the IM column store should be populated. This column has a value only when the corresponding INMEMORY_SERVICE is USER_DEFINED. In all other cases, this column is null.

memoptimize_read.description: ndicates whether the table is enabled for Fast Key Based Access (ENABLED) or not (DISABLED).

pct_used.description: Minimum percentage of used space in a block; NULL for partitioned tables.

max_trans.description: Maximum number of transactions; NULL for partitioned tables.

next_extent.description: Size of secondary extents (in bytes); NULL for partitioned tables.
